hardware_summary: No on-site generation at the terminal; the LNG receiving terminal (Dala Township, west bank of the Yangon River) is a stand-alone regas facility linked by a 24.9 km underground gas pipeline to the separate 388 MW Ahlone combined-cycle power plant (2x128.5 MW gas turbines + 1x131 MW steam turbine) on the east bank, whose output is sold to the grid via a 28 km 230kV line.
fuel_basis: n/a - direction test, not a fuel-gate case
captive_summary: This is a classic LNG-to-power direction-test case: the terminal exists solely to pipe regasified gas to the separate Ahlone CCPP, which sells power to EPGE/the grid. No source describes any on-site generation serving the terminal's own regas/pumping load. Design confirmed by TTCL's own ESIA filing and independent trade press.
confirmed_how: TTCL Power Myanmar's ESIA (hosted on Open Development Myanmar) states: "The Natural Gas Pipeline (24.9 km), which will transfer natural gas (NG) from the LNG Receiving Terminal to the Power Plant, will run through Dala, Seikgyikanaungto, and Ahlone Townships" -- confirming the terminal and power plant are separate sites linked by pipeline, gas flowing OUT of the terminal. NaturalGasWorld corroborates: the 388 MW facility "will be attached to a 28-km power line, a 25-km gas pipeline and LNG receiving terminal."
